candidates.source_body_excerpt: Bury Beer Festival will return to The Met’s historic Derby Hall for two days in November. Breweries from Bury and across the North West will serve a range of beers at the venue’s biggest annual fundraiser. The festival will bring cask, keg and small-batch beers into Derby Hall, with styles including IPAs and stouts. Five breweries have been announced so far: Brightside Brewing Company, Brewsmith Beer, Tun Brewing Company, Wakey Wakey Brew Company and Vocation Brewery. The Met says more names will follow. Beer will not be the only option. A cider and perry bar will sit alongside a selection of gins, wines and cocktails, while non-alcoholic drinks will also be available. Fratelli’s will serve New York-style pizza throughout the event. Local DJs are scheduled to play across the weekend as visitors meet the brewers, try different drinks and spend time with friends. The Met says it will not use plastic glasses as part of its efforts to reduce the festival’s environmental impact. Visitors will instead be able to pick up a branded festival glass on the day. The venue has also asked visitors to plan their journeys and drink responsibly. There is a taxi bay outside The Met, and nearby parking is available for those travelling with a designated driver. Bury Beer Festival is The Met’s biggest annual fundraiser. The registered charity says ticket proceeds help support its work with local communities, artists and audiences. Do you have a story for us? candidates.source_body_excerpt: Four arrests were made as police seized drugs worth an estimated £1 million in a series of raids at dawn in Rochdale on Monday. Greater Manchester Police said the swoops followed a six month-long probe into a 'suspected large-scale supply and distribution of illicit drugs'. Detectives said they believe the operation was 'supplying drugs both online and in person to customers nationally'. Officers from GMP's Serious Organised Crime Group (SOCG), supported by the Tactical Aid Unit, executed six warrants across the town. The premises targeted, said police, were equipped with security measures. Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter The force said it uncovered what is believed to be a 'dedicated drugs storage facility' on Manchester Road, Rochdale. A 'vast quantity' of suspected drugs were subsequently found inside, GMP added. Police said a list detailing more than 100 different types of drugs - ranging across Class A, B and C - were discovered, with a 'significant proportion' of the haul said to be prescription-type medication alongside bodybuilding and weight-loss drugs. A number of electronic devices were also seized, including more than 30 mobile phones, with an estimated £60,000 in cash recovered. Two men aged 52 and 23 were arrested on Twinegate, Rochdale, with a man aged 51 also arrested on Whittaker Lane, Rochdale. The fourth suspect, a man aged 44, was arrested on Kingsway. All four were held on suspicion of conspiracy to supply Class A, B and C drugs and remained in custody on Monday afternoon. Detective Inspector Rich McCorry, from GMP's Serious Organised Crime Group, said the investigation, codenamed 'Nostalgic', would continue. "Let this be a clear message to anyone choosing to involve themselves in serious and organised crime. Greater Manchester Police will not stand for it and we will find you. We will work relentlessly to disrupt the lifestyle your criminality is funding. "We believe this is a sophisticated and well-established organised crime group. The premises we entered today were fully equipped with security measures, laptops and large quantities of drugs, indicating what we suspect was a highly organised operation supplying drugs both online and in person to customers nationally. "This type of criminality fuels violence, exploitation and misery in our communities, while those responsible seek to profit from it. We are determined to dismantle these networks."

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Police have seized an estimated £1 million worth of drugs and arrested four people as part of an investigation into the suspected large-scale supply and distribution of illicit drugs. Officers from the Serious Organised Crime Group (SOCG), supported by the Tactical Aid Unit (TAU), executed six warrants across Rochdale this morning. Over the past six months, officers have worked to build a detailed intelligence picture, using surveillance, telecommunications data and a range of investigative enquiries to establish the scale of the suspected drugs network and identify those believed to be involved. That work led officers to several premises believed to be linked to the storage and distribution of illicit drugs on a significant commercial scale. During this morning’s warrants, officers uncovered what is suspected to be a dedicated drugs storage facility in Manchester Road, Rochdale. From the outside, the address appeared to be a residential property, but inside officers discovered vast quantities of suspected illicit drugs with an estimated value of more than £1 million. Officers also discovered a list detailing more than 100 different types of drugs believed to have been supplied by the organised crime group, ranging across Class A, B and C drugs. A significant proportion of the haul consisted of prescription-type medication, alongside bodybuilding and weight-loss drugs.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Dr Helen Palmer has been appointed independent Chair of Rochdale Creates, the borough’s Cultural Compact. The partnership brings together organisations and individuals working in culture, education, business and the community. Dr Palmer has more than 30 years’ experience in culture, heritage, tourism and partnership development. She has previously worked with Touchstones Rochdale, Rochdale Borough Council and Rochdale Development Agency. As Chair, she will lead the partnership’s governance and help its members work together on cultural projects across the borough. Dr Palmer, who runs the consultancy Palmer Squared and is Co Chair of What Next? Greater Manchester, said: “Rochdale has developed an ambitious and compelling vision for culture, built on strong partnerships, rich heritage and a growing creative sector. I am excited to support Rochdale Creates as it enters its next phase and to work alongside partners across the borough to help turn that ambition into action.” Rochdale Creates was established in 2022. Its members include artists, cultural organisations, educators, businesses, community groups and public sector partners. Councillor Sue Smith, Rochdale Borough Council’s Cabinet Member for Communities and Cooperation, said: “We are delighted to welcome Helen as Chair of Rochdale Creates. This is a significant appointment for the borough's cultural sector and reflects how far the Cultural Compact has come since it was established three years ago. Attracting someone of Helen's calibre, profile and experience demonstrates the strength of Rochdale's cultural and creative sector and the exciting opportunities that exist here.”

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Hopwood Hall College has introduced new student uniforms supplied by Rochdale-based ICON Sports for the academic year. Students across both campuses are wearing the kit, and some tutors have received branded workwear. ICON Sports makes custom sportswear and workwear. The college said it selected the company following a procurement and evaluation process, with its local base among the factors considered. The uniforms are intended for students studying vocational qualifications, including T Levels. Tutors in the college’s Advanced Manufacturing and Technology Centre are among the staff wearing the new workwear. Julia Heap OBE, Principal and CEO of Hopwood Hall College, said: “The new term has started with a bang and there’s a fantastic energy across our campuses – partly because of the new uniforms! “The students have wasted no time embracing the new kit, which is certainly the right gear for success. “It’s been a great experience working alongside ICON Sports to ensure that the next generation look the part as they gain life-changing qualifications. “We’re delighted to have this opportunity to partner with a growing local business and to further invest in the economy of Rochdale.”

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale Council has launched a “Stop Means Stop” campaign to remind drivers to stop for school crossing patrols. It says parking enforcement patrols outside schools will also increase. Councillor Dylan Williams, the council’s cabinet member for Highways and Facilities, launched the campaign at St Luke’s Primary School in Heywood. The council said it recorded 137 instances of drivers failing to stop outside schools over the past five years, including cases where a crossing patrol had already stepped into the road. “There have been multiple cases across the borough and across Greater Manchester with cars not stopping for the lollipop people,” Cllr Williams said. “This is obviously a real danger for schoolchildren across the borough. It’s really important that people stop.” The council is also asking drivers to keep yellow lines and school keep-clear markings free of parked vehicles. Cllr Williams said the increased parking patrols would take place without a fixed schedule. A crossing patrol worker at St Luke’s, identified as Chris, said vehicles parked on zigzag lines obstructed both his view and the view of passing drivers. candidates.source_body_excerpt: The former Kingsway Hotel pub at 125 Kingsway, Rochdale, is being marketed for £425,000. The listing says the site could be considered for residential or retail use, subject to planning permission. The two-storey building sits on a 0.44-acre site and has about 4,050 sq ft of ground-floor space. The first floor includes a function room and a three-bedroom private flat. There is also a surfaced car park with space for approximately 25 vehicles. Commercial property agent Fleurets describes the building as having brick walls, a roof with distinctive green glazed tiles, and single-storey additions to the sides and rear. The listing gives the total space available as 9,225 sq ft and an asking price equivalent to £46.07 per sq ft. The report says it was built in 1938 and retains historic interior features, including a revolving entrance door, wood panelling and fixed seating. The property is currently advertised as a pub for sale. Fleurets says other uses may be possible, subject to planning permission. No change of use has been announced in the material supplied. candidates.source_body_excerpt: A landmark Rochdale pub which has been vacant for eight years is on the market in a bid to give it a new lease of life. The Kingsway Hotel, at 125 Kingsway, Rochdale, closed in July, 2018, and is now on the market through Fleurets estate agents with a price of £425,000. Fleurets is marketing the property as suitable for residential or retail use, subject to planning permission. As well as the pub and dining areas downstairs, upstairs includes a three-bedroom private flat and function room. The former pub was built in 1938 and visitors to it described the interior as “stepping back in time”. Original features remain intact. Image: Rightmove/Fleurets It’s CAMRA listing reads: “Dating from 1938 this pub has four rooms, a further room upstairs, and it very little altered with only the off-sales removed. “The entrance on Kingsway retains its original revolving door and leads to a large lobby bar with parquet floor, plain skylight, and original fixed seating.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Councillor Lee Wolf has called for an urgent meeting with police and council officers over reports of disorder in Middleton town centre and at the former Durnford Street School site. In a post to a local Facebook group, Councillor Wolf said he was requesting a meeting of the Middleton Township Committee with Greater Manchester Police and senior council officers. “Our town cannot become a no-go zone for residents,” he wrote. “We need immediate action taken to disperse these groups and an increased police presence on our streets.” In a separate public post, he alleged that groups of young people were entering the former school site daily and climbing onto its roof. He said stones and mud had been thrown at passing and parked cars, and claimed that some parents had dropped children off at the site. Councillor Wolf said the building was not properly secured and criticised the property owners’ response. He said he was speaking to council officers about enforcement action and called for cameras at the site, including cameras capable of recording vehicle registration plates. He urged residents to report every incident to police so there would be an official record. People responding to his town centre post described further concerns. Tracey Kelly said she had nearly been hit by someone riding a bike while wearing a balaclava and alleged that fireworks had been directed towards shops and cars. Trisha Catherine said fireworks had been set off in bins outside a town centre business on a previous Saturday night. Michelle Jarvis described young people throwing fireworks and entering and leaving food shops near Tesco. Another commenter alleged that objects had been thrown at staff inside McDonald’s.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: A monthly group for neurodivergent people, families and carers in Prestwich is marking its first anniversary in September. Michelle Mackin, a care co-ordinator working with Bury GP Federation and local GP practices, set up Different Minds, One Community after seeing a need for a place where people could find advice and meet others. The group meets at The Woodthorpe on Bury Old Road. Michelle said it brings together support from social prescribing staff and community groups. Dominic Burke, who has experienced severe food anxiety for more than a decade, said attending the group had helped him find support for his health and search for work. “The group has given me somewhere to go and meet other people in smaller groups, know I will be supported, and get advice,” he said. He has also taken part in activities at Prestwich’s Creative Living Centre and received CV guidance. Maxine Ackerley, a parent of neurodivergent children, said meeting other parents and carers had helped her share experiences and find advice. “This group gives you somewhere to come and be heard and helped,” she said. Different Minds, One Community meets on the second Wednesday of each month from 1.30pm to 3pm at The Woodthorpe, Bury Old Road, Prestwich M25 0EG. candidates.source_body_excerpt: A campaign has been launched to keep children safe by reminding drivers they have to stop for school crossing patrols. The drive was launched last week at St Luke’s Primary School in Heywood. As well as getting across the Stop Means Stop message, parking wardens will be on patrol outside schools to enforce restrictions. Rochdale Council shared: “We know that life is busy and we all need to get to places fast, but now the kids are back in school, it’s more important than ever that we take it slow and leave space around schools. “There were 137 fail to stops outside schools over the past five years, with people driving straight through, even after our school crossing patrols had stepped into the road. Cllr Dylan Williams launches the Stop Means Stop campaign at St Luke’s Primary School in Heywood. candidates.source_body_excerpt: Greater Manchester Police officers attended an address on Tweedale Street in Rochdale at approximately 4 p.m. on Monday, 25 May 2026, following reports of a concern for welfare. Officers discovering the 44-year-old woman deceased at the scene initiated immediate contact with ambulance services, though medical personnel could only confirm the victim’s death rather than undertake resuscitative measures. The initial incident classification reflected uncertainty regarding the cause of death, with responding officers treating the circumstances as potentially suspicious rather than immediately declaring murder investigation protocols. However, subsequent examination and preliminary forensic assessment rapidly escalated the investigation to full murder inquiry status. Detective senior investigating officers commenced immediate containment procedures, establishing crime scene security and preserving evidence for later forensic examination. Specialist teams from Greater Manchester Police’s Major Incident Team assumed investigative responsibilities, utilising established protocols for homicide inquiries. Kyle Howard, aged 25 years old and residing at the same Tweedale Street property where the victim was discovered, was arrested on suspicion of murder within hours of the police response. Howard’s presence at the address and circumstantial evidence established through immediate neighbourhood canvassing and witness interviews accelerated suspect identification significantly. By 3 June 2026, eight days following the initial discovery, Greater Manchester Police confirmed that Howard had been charged with murder and remanded in custody pending court proceedings. His appearance at Manchester Magistrates Court on 3 June 2026 formalised the charge, with the defendant remanded in custody pending further court appearances and trial preparation. Greater Manchester Police characterised the investigation as complete regarding the immediate arrest phase, though ongoing inquiries continued regarding potential additional circumstances or contributing factors surrounding the death. Greater Manchester Police’s Major Incident Team operates structured investigative frameworks encompassing witness identification, forensic evidence preservation, and secure evidence chain management. Following death notification to next of kin, supported by specialist family liaison officers, investigators establish timeline reconstructions, witness statement gathering, and preliminary forensic assessment protocols. Detective Chief Inspector Liz Hopkinson, of Greater Manchester Police’s Major Incident Team, told investigators that “this is a tragic set of circumstances where a woman has lost her life, and we have a team of dedicated officers working around the clock to establish what happened.” The characterisation reflects the emotional gravity of homicide investigations whilst emphasising systematic investigative commitment.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Vale of Lune’s winning streak continued as they kicked off the new season with Saturday’s 32-28 victory at Rochdale, writes BARRY LEES. The first XV’s first meaningful encounter of the NW1 adventure had seen livewire flanker Sam Walton leave early for treatment to an eye injury. Reorganising ensued and the skill set of the crew on the bench began to kick in. Rochdale stepped up production and pressed into the Vale 22, where they powered over the tryline to open the scoring. They soon added a second to reinforce their intent as Alex Ryder came on to bolster Vale’s forward effort. From a sustained period of possession, Jordan Dorrington made the crucial break for Ben McGarvey to strike in the right corner. However, Mike Bradshaw infringed the rucking rules and was dispatched for a breather. It was time for Vale to dig deep and Eddie Abdelghafar led the backs’ charge, earning a chance for Jamie Mayall to slot over a penalty kick which left Vale six points behind the home team at the break, trailing 14-8. With Alex Briggs making a welcome return to first-team rugby after injury, a high clearance from the Vale fell to Rochdale’s nippy centre. They darted through the gaps to set up the next Rochdale try before more Vale changes saw Ben Gould come on for his debut in place of scrum-half Matty Kaye. A Rochdale foot in touch was flagged by the touch judge but overruled by the referee, with the resulting possession setting off a passing phase across the pitch for their fourth try of the afternoon. Sam Wallbank also transgressed the tackling laws, which meant he headed for the bench. With 17 points in it, a man down and 15 minutes remaining on the clock, it was no time for the faint-hearted. The Vale squad showed it is anything but that, starting with the flamboyant Jack Macfarlane pulling a try back and Mayall adding the garnish. Grafting together with increased energy, the Vale pack enabled prop Tadgh Butler to register his first try for the club. Three points behind and with the bit between their teeth, Vale rose in confidence and cancelled out all of Rochdale’s earlier advantages. The final word was delivered in the form of a relentless spell of Vale forward possession, well past 80 minutes, in the Rochdale 22. The ball was moved out to McGarvey, who then finished under the posts. Amidst the visiting crowd’s jubilation, Mayall - sporting a head bandage - kicked the conversion for Vale, whose first home fixture of the season comes against Leek RUFC on Saturday (3pm). Vale of Lune: Crompton, Verlaque, Butler, Sutcliffe, Procter, Walton, Ayrton, Wallbank, Kaye, Clifton, McGarvey, Mayall, Abdelghafar, Macfarlane, Dorrington. Replacements: Bradshaw, Taylor-Smith, Ryder, Briggs, Gould.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale AFC Community Trust will hold its annual sleep out at the Crown Oil Arena on Friday 9 October 2026. The event has been renamed the Change Lives Sleep Out to raise funds for its Changing Lives programme. The Trust held its first Rochdale Sleep Out with Petrus on 29 August 2025. Together, the two organisations raised £7,875.52. The Trust used its share of the money to help establish Changing Lives, a programme run in partnership with Petrus Housing for people experiencing homelessness or living in supported accommodation. The Trust says Changing Lives has supported 33 people in its first eight months. It offers free football alongside wellbeing, personal development and employability activities. Its aim is to give participants a place to meet others, improve their physical and mental wellbeing, and find routes into volunteering, education or work. During those eight months, the programme has held 28 football and engagement sessions, five specialist workshops and four free haircut sessions. Participants have played two competitive football fixtures and attended two Rochdale AFC first-team matches. When the partnership was announced in December 2025, Scott Webster, the Trust’s deputy director, said it would give people “the chance to improve their health and well-being, develop a sense of community and belonging, and gain valuable skills for future progression.” This year’s sleep out invites individuals, families, businesses, schools and community groups to spend a night under the floodlights at the Crown Oil Arena. People can join on their own or as part of a group. Those unable to take part can donate. The Trust says the event is intended to support people affected by homelessness, rather than recreate their experience. Money raised will help continue Changing Lives and offer its activities to more people. People can sign up or donate through the event page .

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Ten-man Rochdale survived a Fleetwood onslaught to earn a 2-1 victory at Highbury. The visitors raced into a two-goal lead inside 14 minutes, Dajaune Brown netting with a first-time finish from Glenn Middleton’s cross in the eighth minute before Aden Flint doubled Dale’s advantage, coolly slotting home after Brown’s shot fell kindly into his path. Mark Helm hit back on the half-hour mark, pouncing on a loose ball in midfield and finishing neatly into the bottom corner. Fleetwood pushed hard for an equaliser, with Ched Evans’ shot deflected inches wide, Raffaele Cirino hitting the side-netting and Aaron Loupalo-Bi narrowly wide with a fierce low drive. The home side dominated the second half but Lewis McCann clearing the bar by inches was as close as they got. Dale’s task got even tougher on 69 minutes when Tobi Adebayo-Rowling received a second yellow card for a shirt pull. Goalkeeper Sam Waller then denied Evans and Flint got his head to Ronan Coughlan’s goalbound shot as valiant defending, and Fleetwood’s wayward finishing, saw Dale hold on for the win.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: A Middleton woman who stopped drinking in 2019 says writing horror stories has helped her explore her experiences of addiction and trauma. Alex Herod said she tried meetings, therapy, books and sober communities before she began writing fiction as part of her recovery. She has a diagnosis of complex PTSD and is now working on a creative writing PhD about the role horror writing plays in her own recovery. “Although I write fiction, most of my stories relate back to themes of addiction, trauma, mental health, transformation and recovery,” she said. “Writing horror has allowed me to go into very dark places and come out the other side. I can explore feelings of disgust and monstrousness - how I felt about myself when I was drinking, or how I felt others saw me - and do so in a way that is in my control.” Alex said being able to edit and rewrite a story gives her a way to express experiences she previously felt unable to discuss. She described the process as “making friends with my monsters”. “It helps me to process my experiences of addiction and trauma, and learn to accept and embrace the darker parts of myself so I don’t feel disconnected,” she said. Alex, who works at the University of Salford, is due to release her debut novel next year. Goals from Dajaune Brown and Aden Flint put Dale 2-0 up early on but they were forced into sterling rearguard action in the second half, especially after Tobi Adebayo-Rowling saw a second yellow card 21 minutes from time, with Mark Helm having reduced the deficit. I felt the first 20 was really pleasing, then I think we maybe played the scoreboard a little bit after that and self-preservation mode kicked in a little bit. “We got to half-time and I thought we regrouped, and started the second half really well. There’s so much I love about today’s performance, not just with the ball, but everything without the ball, and the heart and desire the boys showed as well. “I understand where the frustration comes from but my responsibility is to not listen to any noise, just focus and back myself as a coach, as a human as well. My mentality is strong and I believe in myself. But how amazing were the fans as well, they got us over the line.” Fleetwood manager Matt Lawlor cut a frustrated figure having seen his side start slowly and then fail to break Dale down for an equaliser.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Ten-man Rochdale survived a Fleetwood onslaught to earn a 2-1 victory at Highbury. The visitors raced into a two-goal lead inside 14 minutes, Dajaune Brown netting with a first-time finish from Glenn Middleton's cross in the eighth minute before Aden Flint doubled Dale's advantage, coolly slotting home after Brown's shot fell kindly into his path. Mark Helm hit back on the half-hour mark, pouncing on a loose ball in midfield and finishing neatly into the bottom corner. Fleetwood pushed hard for an equaliser, with Ched Evans' shot deflected inches wide, Raffaele Cirino hitting the side-netting and Aaron Loupalo-Bi narrowly wide with a fierce low drive. The home side dominated the second half but Lewis McCann clearing the bar by inches was as close as they got. Dale's task got even tougher on 69 minutes when Tobi Adebayo-Rowling received a second yellow card for a shirt pull. Goalkeeper Sam Waller then denied Evans and Flint got his head to Ronan Coughlan's goalbound shot as valiant defending, and Fleetwood's wayward finishing, saw Dale hold on for the win. candidates.source_body_excerpt: A mayoral charity coffee morning at The Mill About on Friday 25 September raised £660 for the Mayoral Charity Fund. The Christie is one of the charities it supports. Alison and the team at The Mill About hosted the event. Adam George from The Christie joined the Mayor, Mayoress, Mayoral Team and volunteers. Mayor Councillor Faisal Rana, thanked those who attended and donated. Speaking to Roch Valley Radio, he said: “Raising £660 at this morning’s coffee morning is a fantastic achievement, and I am incredibly grateful to everyone who attended, donated and supported the event. The money raised will go towards my Mayoral Charities, of which The Christie is one. I would like to thank my Mayoral Team, Alison and the team at The Mill About, and Adam George from The Christie for helping make this event possible. Cancer affects so many families, and supporting vital research, improving treatments and raising awareness is so important. This wonderful community effort shows how, together, we can make a real difference to people’s lives.” The Mayoress, Iram Faisal, speaking to Roch Valley Radio, said the event also gave people an opportunity to learn about the charities supported by the fund.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Ten-man Rochdale survived a Fleetwood onslaught to earn a 2-1 victory at Highbury. The visitors raced into a two-goal lead inside 14 minutes, Dajaune Brown netting with a first-time finish from Glenn Middleton’s cross in the eighth minute before Aden Flint doubled Dale’s advantage, coolly slotting home after Brown’s shot fell kindly into his path. Mark Helm hit back on the half-hour mark, pouncing on a loose ball in midfield and finishing neatly into the bottom corner. Fleetwood pushed hard for an equaliser, with Ched Evans’ shot deflected inches wide, Raffaele Cirino hitting the side-netting and Aaron Loupalo-Bi narrowly wide with a fierce low drive. The home side dominated the second half but Lewis McCann clearing the bar by inches was as close as they got. Dale’s task got even tougher on 69 minutes when Tobi Adebayo-Rowling received a second yellow card for a shirt pull. Goalkeeper Sam Waller then denied Evans and Flint got his head to Ronan Coughlan’s goalbound shot as valiant defending, and Fleetwood’s wayward finishing, saw Dale hold on for the win.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: A murder investigation has been launched after a man died following an incident in Rochdale in the early hours of this morning. At around 1.30am, Greater Manchester Police officers responded to reports of an assault in South Parade in Rochdale, where a man, aged 52, was found unconscious. He was taken to hospital for treatment but, despite the best efforts of emergency services, he sadly died. Two men have been arrested in connection with the incident and remain in custody for questioning. Detectives from the Major Incident Team are now leading the investigation and are appealing for anyone who witnessed the incident, has information about what happened, or has relevant CCTV, mobile phone or dashcam footage to come forward. The victim’s family are being supported by specialist officers. Detective Chief Inspector Claire Brennan, from the Major Incident Team, said : “This is a heart-breaking incident in which a man has tragically lost his life. “Our thoughts are first and foremost with his family and loved ones who are being supported by specially trained officers at this incredibly difficult time.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale secured a 2-1 victory over Fleetwood Town at Highbury Stadium on September 26, 2026, despite playing the final 21 minutes with ten men following Tobi Adebayo-Rowling's dismissal.Dajaune Brown opened the scoring for the visiting side in the eighth minute with a right-footed finish from the center of the penalty area. Aden Flint doubled Rochdale's advantage six minutes later, striking into the bottom-left corner after Brown blocked an initial effort.Mark Helm brought Fleetwood Town back into the contest in the 30th minute. The midfielder received a pass from Aaron Loupalo-Bi outside the box and drove a right-footed shot into the bottom-right corner of the net.Fleetwood Town pushed for an equalizer before the break, but Rochdale goalkeeper Sam Waller maintained the visitors' lead by saving a header from captain Ched Evans and a tight-angle effort from Raff Cirino.Rochdale was reduced to ten players in the 69th minute when Adebayo-Rowling received a second yellow card for a foul on Loupalo-Bi. Fleetwood Town capitalized on the numerical advantage to create multiple opportunities in the closing stages.Waller made several key saves during the second half to deny Evans, Ronan Coughlan, and Lewis McCann. Fleetwood Town was unable to find a second goal despite five minutes of added time.Fleetwood Town manager Matt Lawlor adjusted his squad during the match, introducing Jake Batty for Kayden Hughes in the 64th minute and Coughlan for Adam Murphy in the 70th minute.

The visitors raced into a two-goal lead inside 14 minutes, Dajaune Brown netting with a first-time finish from Glenn Middleton’s cross in the eighth minute before Aden Flint doubled Dale’s advantage, coolly slotting home after Brown’s shot fell kindly into his path. Mark Helm hit back on the half-hour mark, pouncing on a loose ball in midfield and finishing neatly into the bottom corner. Fleetwood pushed hard for an equaliser, with Ched Evans’ shot deflected inches wide, Raffaele Cirino hitting the side-netting and Aaron Loupalo-Bi narrowly wide with a fierce low drive. The home side dominated the second half but Lewis McCann clearing the bar by inches was as close as they got. Dale’s task got even tougher on 69 minutes when Tobi Adebayo-Rowling received a second yellow card for a shirt pull. Goalkeeper Sam Waller then denied Evans and Flint got his head to Ronan Coughlan’s goalbound shot as valiant defending, and Fleetwood’s wayward finishing, saw Dale hold on for the win.
